S3 ~line 38 - The set_verbosity row says 'UVM_INFO lines are hidden when v is above the run's verbosity'. In uvm-core, print_msg and the summary call uvm_report(sev, ..., get_verbosity()), and uvm_report_enabled filters on verbosity for every severity. So a MISCMP line raised to UVM_ERROR is also hidden, and it then does not count in the error total. That interaction affects the severity row. -> Write 'MISCMP lines (of any severity) are hidden...' and add to the severity row 'only lines that pass the verbosity filter print and count'.

S3 ~line 42 - 'Only the last row can turn a passing compare() into a failing one' is odd for set_check_type. It already defaults to 1, so calling the knob can only make a failing compare pass (set_check_type(0)), and in uvm-core even that is undone by the flush() at the start of compare(). -> Write 'Only the type check can change the return value; the knob itself can only switch it off, and uvm-core's flush() turns it back on.'

findings: S2 line 160 - The set_threshold(n) row of the 'What each knob can change' matrix says 'a hand-written do_compare is not gated'. That is false for a do_compare written with the `uvm_compare_* macros: m_uvm_compare_threshold_begin wraps them too (uvm-core uvm_comparer_defines.svh, lines 45-59 and 91). It also contradicts the lesson's own knob table at line 149 and the one-glance summary, which both say the threshold stops the field macros and the `uvm_compare_* macros. Only direct compare_field_* calls skip the gate. -> Reword the cell to: 'direct compare_field_* calls in a hand-written do_compare are not gated (the `uvm_compare_* macros are)'.

S3 line 164 - The set_check_type(b) row presents the type check as a knob that can make compare() return 0. In uvm-core, flush() at the start of compare() sets check_type back to 1, so set_check_type(0) never takes effect through compare(). The row really describes the default behaviour, and only the note at line 169 says so. -> Start the row with 'The default 1:' or add '(uvm-core: always 1 inside compare())' in the first cell, so a reader of the row alone is not misled.

S3 line 37 - The ArchitectureDiagram caption says 'Read it top to bottom', but do_compare (the step labelled 2nd) sits at row 1 to the right of the policy, while do_execute_op (1st) sits below at row 2.
